name: Elin Johansson
headline: 35-year-old owner of a printing shop in Stockholm
title: After-Work Invitation
situation: Elin is packing up her things in the office at the printing plant when her phone buzzes. It's a message from Lukas, a fellow business owner she sometimes chats with at chamber of commerce breakfasts. He says a few of them are meeting at a pub near the square in half an hour and invites her to join. She has no pressing tasks at the factory, and her mother's evening aide has already confirmed the shift. She pauses, thinking about the warm pub noise and the cold car seat waiting in the lot.

context.relationship_profiles: Lukas runs a packaging supplier and has exchanged referrals with Elin at two chamber breakfasts. They have never met outside business events. Last quarter he introduced her to a cosmetics buyer who later placed a small order.
context.tendencies: When work is under control, Elin occasionally stays late to clean the solvent tanks or update the customer list; she rarely leaves early for social plans. She has declined three similar last-minute pub invitations in the past year.
context.current_state: Her shoulders ache from hauling a carton of samples to shipping. The factory intercom is silent. She is aware of the empty parking lot through the window.
context.immediate_memories: The chamber's Christmas gathering where Lukas told a story about a misprinted label and she laughed more than she expected. That same evening her mother’s aide texted a photo of her mother smiling.
context.reflective_memories: Her father used to say that a handshake sealed a deal better than a drink, but he also kept a bottle of aquavit in his desk for the older press operators after a hard run.
